claim: Peripheral nerves are organ-like structures containing diverse cell types to optimize function.
source: Peripheral nerves are organ-like structures containing diverse cell types to optimize function.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the composition of peripheral nerves.

claim: Peripheral nerves include mostly axon-associated Schwann cells.
source: This interactive assembly includes mostly axon-associated Schwann cells, but also endothelial cells of supporting blood vessels, immune system-associated cells, barrier-forming cells of the perineurium surrounding and protecting nerve fascicles, and connective tissue-resident cells within the intra-fascicular endoneurium and inter-fascicular epineurium.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states that Schwann cells are the predominant cell type in peripheral nerves.

claim: Peripheral nerves contain endothelial cells of supporting blood vessels.
source: This interactive assembly includes mostly axon-associated Schwann cells, but also endothelial cells of supporting blood vessels, immune system-associated cells, barrier-forming cells of the perineurium surrounding and protecting nerve fascicles, and connective tissue-resident cells within the intra-fascicular endoneurium and inter-fascicular epineurium.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly lists endothelial cells as one of the cell types present in peripheral nerves.

claim: Peripheral nerves contain immune system-associated cells.
source: This interactive assembly includes mostly axon-associated Schwann cells, but also endothelial cells of supporting blood vessels, immune system-associated cells, barrier-forming cells of the perineurium surrounding and protecting nerve fascicles, and connective tissue-resident cells within the intra-fascicular endoneurium and inter-fascicular epineurium.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly lists immune system-associated cells as one of the cell types present in peripheral nerves.

claim: Peripheral nerves contain barrier-forming cells of the perineurium that surround and protect nerve fascicles.
source: This interactive assembly includes mostly axon-associated Schwann cells, but also endothelial cells of supporting blood vessels, immune system-associated cells, barrier-forming cells of the perineurium surrounding and protecting nerve fascicles, and connective tissue-resident cells within the intra-fascicular endoneurium and inter-fascicular epineurium.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes perineurial cells and their barrier-forming function.

claim: Peripheral nerves contain connective tissue-resident cells within the intra-fascicular endoneurium and inter-fascicular epineurium.
source: This interactive assembly includes mostly axon-associated Schwann cells, but also endothelial cells of supporting blood vessels, immune system-associated cells, barrier-forming cells of the perineurium surrounding and protecting nerve fascicles, and connective tissue-resident cells within the intra-fascicular endoneurium and inter-fascicular epineurium.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly lists connective tissue-resident cells in specific nerve compartments.

claim: The study combined bulk RNA sequencing of developing sciatic nerves up to the adult stage.
source: To achieve this goal, we have combined bulk RNA sequencing of developing sciatic nerves up to the adult with focused bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing of Schwann cells throughout postnatal development, extended by single-cell transcriptome analysis of the full sciatic nerve both perinatally and in the adult.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The study performed focused bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing of Schwann cells throughout postnatal development.
source: To achieve this goal, we have combined bulk RNA sequencing of developing sciatic nerves up to the adult with focused bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing of Schwann cells throughout postnatal development, extended by single-cell transcriptome analysis of the full sciatic nerve both perinatally and in the adult.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The study performed single-cell transcriptome analysis of the full sciatic nerve both perinatally and in the adult.
source: To achieve this goal, we have combined bulk RNA sequencing of developing sciatic nerves up to the adult with focused bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing of Schwann cells throughout postnatal development, extended by single-cell transcriptome analysis of the full sciatic nerve both perinatally and in the adult.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The results were merged in the transcriptome resource Sciatic Nerve ATlas (SNAT) at https://www.snat.ethz.ch.
source: The results were merged in the transcriptome resource Sciatic Nerve ATlas (SNAT: https://www.snat.ethz.ch).
evidence: The abstract explicitly states where the data resource is available.

claim: Peripheral nerves are specialized in the transport of information between the central nervous system and peripheral body parts, including muscles and sensory cells.
source: Peripheral nerves are specialized in the transport of information between the central nervous system and peripheral body parts, including muscles and sensory cells (Stassart et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Stassart et al., 2018.

claim: The function of peripheral nerves is mainly fulfilled by axons/neurons in symbiosis with interacting Schwann cells.
source: This function is mainly fulfilled by axons/neurons in symbiosis with interacting Schwann cells (SCs).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the primary functional components of peripheral nerves.

claim: Cells expressing Pdgfra include endoneurial, perineurial, and epineural cells.
source: This group includes cells expressing Pdgfra (encoding Platelet Derived Growth Factor Receptor Alpha) such as endoneurial, perineurial, and epineural cells (also designated as fibroblast-like or mesenchymal cells [Carr et al., 2019; Joseph et al., 2004; Ma et al., 2018])
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Carr et al., 2019; Joseph et al., 2004; Ma et al., 2018.

claim: Endoneurial, perineurial, and epineural cells are also designated as fibroblast-like or mesenchymal cells.
source: This group includes cells expressing Pdgfra (encoding Platelet Derived Growth Factor Receptor Alpha) such as endoneurial, perineurial, and epineural cells (also designated as fibroblast-like or mesenchymal cells [Carr et al., 2019; Joseph et al., 2004; Ma et al., 2018])
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Carr et al., 2019; Joseph et al., 2004; Ma et al., 2018.

claim: Vascular cells in peripheral nerves include endothelial cells, pericytes, and vascular smooth muscle cells.
source: vascular cells (such as endothelial cells, pericytes, and vascular smooth muscle cells) (Carr et al., 2019; Stierli et al., 2018; Tserentsoodol et al., 1999)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Carr et al., 2019; Stierli et al., 2018; Tserentsoodol et al., 1999.

claim: Peripheral nerves contain epineurial adipocytes.
source: and epineurial adipocytes (Montani et al., 2018; Nadra et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Montani et al., 2018; Nadra et al., 2012.

claim: Each nerve-resident cell type is expected to express a distinct portfolio of genes at particular levels, depending on the differentiation state during development, degeneration and regeneration after injury, and in aging.
source: Each of the nerve-resident cell types is expected to express a distinct portfolio of genes at particular levels, depending on the differentiation state during development, degeneration and regeneration after injury, and in aging.
evidence: This is a statement about expected gene expression patterns in different cell types and conditions.

claim: Knowledge about gene expression in nerve-resident cell types is fragmentary and often limited in cellular resolution.
source: However, our knowledge in this context is fragmentary and often limited in cellular resolution.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Several transcriptome analyses in mice and rats have been carried out that reflect peripheral nerves as an organ.
source: For example, several transcriptome analyses in mice and rats have been carried out that reflect peripheral nerves as an organ (Arthur-Farraj et al., 2017; D'Antonio et al., 2006; Figlia et al., 2017; Fledrich et al., 2018; Fröb et al., 2019; Gerber et al., 2019; Gökbuget et al., 2018; Kim et al., 2018; Le et al., 2005; Nagarajan et al., 2002; Patzig et al., 2011; Quintes et al., 2016; Ryu et al., 2008; Verheijen et al., 2003)
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous transcriptome studies.

claim: Some proteomics studies have been performed on peripheral nerves.
source: complemented by some proteomics studies (Patzig et al., 2011; Siems et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Patzig et al., 2011; Siems et al., 2020.

claim: Bulk analysis of cellularly heterogenous organs and tissues has limitations and is prone to some misinterpretations.
source: They are also prone to some misinterpretations due to the limitations of bulk analysis of cellularly heterogenous organs and tissues.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of bulk analysis approaches.

claim: Schwann cells are the most numerous cell type present in nerves.
source: Nevertheless, since SCs are the most numerous cell type present in nerves (Stierli et al., 2018), such datasets can be and have been interpreted, at first approximation, as a surrogate for the analysis of SC gene expression.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Stierli et al., 2018.

claim: Bulk analysis datasets of peripheral nerves can be interpreted as a surrogate for the analysis of Schwann cell gene expression.
source: Nevertheless, since SCs are the most numerous cell type present in nerves (Stierli et al., 2018), such datasets can be and have been interpreted, at first approximation, as a surrogate for the analysis of SC gene expression.
evidence: This is an inference based on the predominance of Schwann cells in nerves.

claim: Myelinating and non-myelinating (Remak) Schwann cells are expected to express different subsets of transcripts.
source: Even among SCs, however, this approach cannot resolve the differences between myelinating and non-myelinating (also known as Remak) SCs, which are expected to express different subsets of transcripts (Gomez-Sanchez et al., 2017; Harty and Monk, 2017; Jessen et al., 2015; Monk et al., 2015; Salzer, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Gomez-Sanchez et al., 2017; Harty and Monk, 2017; Jessen et al., 2015; Monk et al., 2015; Salzer, 2015.

claim: Studies analyzing Schwann cells more specifically have been largely restricted to either early embryonic development or adult stages mainly in the context of tissue regeneration after injury.
source: Studies aimed at analyzing SCs more specifically (Clements et al., 2017), and also the transcriptomes of other cell types in the nerve with single-cell RNA sequencing (Carr et al., 2019), have been largely restricted to either early embryonic development (Buchstaller et al., 2004; Furlan et al., 2017) or adult stages mainly in the context of tissue regeneration after injury (Carr et al., 2019; Clements et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The fragmentary time points employed and technical constraints limit the universal use of currently available data.
source: Taken together, the rather fragmentary time points employed, together with some technical constrains, limit the universal use of the currently available data in a satisfactory manner.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of existing data in the field.

claim: Analogous work in the CNS has been highly informative.
source: Thus, motivated by the demands of current research on peripheral nerve biology in health and disease, together with appreciating the highly informative nature of analogous work in the CNS (Marques et al., 2018; Marques et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2014)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Marques et al., 2018; Marques et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2014.

claim: The study analyzed the transcriptome of mouse peripheral nerves by bulk RNA sequencing, with a particular focus on the endoneurium compartment.
source: First, we analyzed the transcriptome of mouse peripheral nerves by bulk RNA sequencing, with a particular focus on the endoneurium compartment, covering a time-line that represents successive stages of nerve development.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The study developed a strategy that allowed the distinction of two fractions of Schwann cells from postnatal day 5 (P5) sciatic nerves by FACS, one enriched in myelinating SCs and another enriched in not-myelinating SCs.
source: Second, we developed a strategy that allowed the distinction of two fractions of SCs from postnatal day 5 (P5) sciatic nerves by FACS, one enriched in myelinating SCs and the another enriched in not-myelinating SCs.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Both fractions of Schwann cells were subjected to bulk RNA sequencing.
source: Both fractions were subjected to bulk RNA sequencing.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The study carried out single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of Schwann cells specifically, collected by FACS at various stages of postnatal differentiation, following the Smart-Seq2 protocol.
source: Third, we carried out single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of SCs specifically, collected by FACS at various stages of postnatal differentiation, following the Smart-Seq2 protocol.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The Smart-Seq2 approach enabled the recapitulation of the myelinating and non-myelinating differentiation trajectories from early development to adult stages at the molecular level.
source: This approach enabled the recapitulation of the myelinating and non-myelinating differentiation trajectories from early development to adult stages at the molecular level.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the results obtained from the Smart-Seq2 approach.

claim: The study used 10x Genomics to extend the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis to the different cell types residing in sciatic nerves, both in perinatal development and in the adult.
source: Finally, we used 10x Genomics to extend the single-cell RNA sequencing analysis to the different cell types residing in sciatic nerves, both in perinatal development and in the adult.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The study extracted nerves from different animals resulting in two independent samples derived from male mice and two independent samples from female mice per each time point.
source: To account for biological diversity, we extracted nerves from different animals resulting in two independent samples derived from male mice and two independent samples from female mice per each time point.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design used in the study.

claim: At embryonic day (E) 13.5, nerves are mainly populated by Schwann cell precursors.
source: The stages analyzed included (a) embryonic day (E) 13.5, when nerves are mainly populated by SC precursors
evidence: This is a direct statement about the developmental stage at E13.5.

claim: At E17.5, P1 and P5, immature Schwann cells gradually sort out individual large caliber axons from axonal bundles and transiently generate pro-myelinating SCs, followed by the onset of myelination.
source: (b) E17.5, P1 and P5, when immature SCs gradually sort out individual large caliber axons from axonal bundles and transiently generate pro-myelinating SCs (i.e. 1:1 relationship of large caliber axons with SCs; not myelinating), followed by the onset of myelination
evidence: This is a direct statement about the developmental stages at E17.5, P1 and P5.

claim: At P14 and P24, radial sorting is completed and the key events ongoing relate to myelin growth and maturation of non-myelinating (Remak) SCs.
source: (c) P14 and P24, when radial sorting is completed and the key events ongoing relate to myelin growth and maturation of non-myelinating (Remak) SCs
evidence: This is a direct statement about the developmental stages at P14 and P24.

claim: At P60, developmental myelination is complete, and non-myelinating SCs together with small caliber axons have formed mature Remak bundles.
source: and (d) P60, a young adult stage in which developmental myelination is complete, and non-myelinating SCs together with small caliber axons have formed mature Remak bundles (Figure 1A; Feltri et al., 2016; Harty and Monk, 2017; Jessen et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Feltri et al., 2016; Harty and Monk, 2017; Jessen et al., 2015.

claim: The temporal synchronization of morphologically recognizable characteristics during peripheral nerve development is only partial, resulting in overlapping features, particularly in early postnatal development.
source: Note that the temporal synchronization of these morphologically recognizable characteristics during peripheral nerve development is only partial, resulting in overlapping features, particularly in early postnatal development.
evidence: This is a statement about the nature of developmental processes in peripheral nerves.

claim: The epineurium and perineurium layers were removed mechanically on samples from E17.5 onwards to extract RNA enriched for the endoneurium compartment.
source: On a relevant technical remark, we removed mechanically the epineurium and perineurium layers as much and as careful as possible on samples from E17.5 onwards to extract RNA enriched for the endoneurium compartment (Jessen et al., 2015; Stierli et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental procedure used in the study.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of the samples, based on the 2000 most variable genes, revealed that the four samples per time point cluster closely together and align to recapitulate the chronological sequence of nerve differentiation.
source: Subsequent hierarchical clustering of the samples, based on the 2000 most variable genes, revealed that the four samples per time point cluster closely together and align to recapitulate the chronological sequence of nerve differentiation (Figure 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Heat map illustrations indicated a gradual transition in the abundance of numerous mRNAs during nerve development, with high consistency between samples.
source: Heat map illustrations indicated a gradual transition in the abundance of numerous mRNAs during nerve development, with high consistency between samples, also apparent in the multidimensional scaling (MDS) plot (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in heat maps and MDS plots.

claim: The proliferation markers Mki67 and Top2a are highly expressed from E17.5 to P5.
source: First, we found as expected that the proliferation markers Mki67 (encoding KI-67) and Top2a (encoding DNA Topoisomerase II Alpha) (Carr et al., 2019; Xie et al., 2018) are highly expressed from E17.5 to P5.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: During E17.5 to P5, radial sorting of axons by Schwann cells destined to myelinate is ongoing and SC proliferation is intense.
source: During this time window, radial sorting of axons by SCs destined to myelinate is ongoing and SC proliferation is intense (Jessen et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Jessen et al., 2015.

claim: As maturation of the nerves proceeds, the expression of proliferation markers decreases.
source: As maturation of the nerves proceeds, the expression of these proliferation markers decreases (Stierli et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Stierli et al., 2018.

claim: Peak expression of Ngfr, Ncam1, and L1cam was found at E17.5, consistent with the high number of immature SCs present in developing nerves at this stage.
source: Second, we assessed the expression of markers typical of immature SCs such as Ngfr (encoding the Low-Affinity Neurotrophin Receptor P75NTR) (Jessen et al., 1990), Ncam1 (encoding the Neural Cell Adhesion Molecule 1) and L1cam (encoding the L1 Neural Cell Adhesion Molecule). Peak expression was found at E17.5, consistent with the high number of immature SCs present in developing nerves at this stage (Jessen et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Expression of Ngfr, Ncam1, and L1cam decreases after E17.5, but remains substantial in agreement with the known expression of these markers also by non-myelinating SCs at later stages.
source: Expression decreases thereafter, but remains substantial in agreement with the known expression of these markers also by non-myelinating SCs at later stages (Faissner et al., 1984; Jessen et al., 2015; Martini and Schachner, 1986; Martini and Schachner, 1988; Nieke and Schachner, 1985).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Highest expression of the pro-myelinating SC marker Pou3f1 was detected at P1 followed by decreasing expression over time.
source: Third, we detected highest expression of the pro-myelinating SC marker Pou3f1 (encoding the Octamer-Binding Transcription Factor 6 (Oct6), also known as SCIP) (Ghazvini et al., 2002; Jessen and Mirsky, 2005; Monuki et al., 1989) at P1 followed by decreasing expression over time, a pattern consistent with comparative morphological analyses (Arroyo et al., 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Expression of Cdkn1c shows a similar peak at P1, in addition to high expression at E13.5.
source: Expression of Cdkn1c (encoding Cyclin-Dependent Kinase Inhibitor 1C (P57, Kip2)) (Heinen et al., 2008) shows a similar peak at P1, in addition to high expression at E13.5.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The levels of transcripts of the myelin protein genes Mpz, Mbp, and Ncmap increase strongly after birth, reflecting the onset of myelination.
source: Fourth, the levels of transcripts of the myelin protein genes Mpz (encoding Myelin Protein Zero), Mbp (encoding Myelin Basic Protein), and Ncmap (encoding Non-Compact Myelin-Associated Protein) (Jessen and Mirsky, 2019; Martini et al., 1988; Patzig et al., 2011; Ryu et al., 2008) increase strongly after birth, reflecting the onset of myelination.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The bulk RNA sequencing dataset provides an accurate transcriptome timeline on postnatal development of the endoneurium compartment of the mouse sciatic nerve.
source: We conclude that this dataset, obtained with bulk RNA sequencing of endoneurium-enriched nerves, provides an accurate transcriptome timeline on postnatal development of the endoneurium compartment of the mouse sciatic nerve and is suitable for appropriate data mining (see SNAT).
evidence: This is a conclusion statement based on the validation of the dataset.

claim: It is an advantage of the bulk RNA sequencing approach that the SCs, as the major cell population in the nerve, together with the other parts of the endoneurium remain in their native context until immediately before RNA extraction.
source: Of technical note, it is an advantage of this approach that the SCs, as the major cell population in the nerve, together with the other parts of the endoneurium remain in their native context until immediately before RNA extraction.
evidence: This is a statement about the technical advantages of the experimental approach.

claim: Keeping cells in their native context minimizes potentially disturbing impacts of experimental procedures and optimizes that the obtained cellular RNA-seq signatures closely track genuine in vivo transcriptomes.
source: This feature minimizes potentially disturbing impacts of experimental procedures and optimizes that the obtained cellular RNA-seq signatures closely track genuine in vivo transcriptomes.
evidence: This is a statement about the technical advantages of the experimental approach.

claim: The study made use of transgenic mice in which SCs were labeled with the eYFP reporter protein in a P0Cre-dependent manner.
source: In particular, we made use of transgenic mice in which SCs were labeled with the eYFP reporter protein (Srinivas et al., 2001) in a P0Cre-dependent manner (Feltri et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental model used in the study.

claim: The mice expressed the dsRed reporter protein under the ubiquitously active chicken beta actin promoter.
source: For consistency with further experiments, the mice expressed also the dsRed reporter protein under the ubiquitously active chicken beta actin promoter (Vintersten et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental model used in the study.

claim: Within the nerves of these animals, SCs express both dsRed and eYFP, while other nerve-resident cells express dsRed only.
source: Within the nerves of these animals, SCs express both dsRed and eYFP, while other nerve-resident cells express dsRed only (Figure 2A).
evidence: This statement is supported by Figure 2A showing the experimental setup.

claim: Analysis by FACS revealed two semi-distinct scatter clouds of eYFP-positive SCs which can be distinguished by different degrees of granularity (SSC-A) values.
source: Analysis by FACS revealed two semi-distinct scatter clouds of eYFP-positive SCs which can be distinguished by different degrees of granularity (SSC-A) values (Figure 2B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The more granular population might relate to myelinating SCs in the nerve, and the less granular population might be enriched in SCs that were not-myelinating at the time of extraction.
source: We hypothesized that these two populations may represent myelinating and not-myelinating SCs, speculating that the more granular population might relate to myelinating SCs in the nerve, and the less granular population might be enriched in SCs that were not-myelinating at the time of extraction.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated by the authors based on their observations.

claim: Heat map and hierarchical clustering analysis revealed high consistency among the differentially regulated transcripts between samples and close clustering of individual replicates within each gating strategy.
source: Heat map and hierarchical clustering analysis revealed high consistency among the differentially regulated transcripts between samples and close clustering of individual replicates within each gating strategy (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The proliferation markers Mki67 and Top2a are strongly elevated in the nmSC gate cells compared to the mSC gate population.
source: The proliferation markers Mki67 and Top2a are strongly elevated in the nmSC gate cells compared to the mSC gate population (Figure 2C), consistent with increased abundance of proliferating immature SCs in the nmSC gate population.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Expression analysis of the immature SC markers Ngfr, Ncam1, and L1cam confirms the strong enrichment of immature SCs in the nmSC gate relative to the mSC gate.
source: Expression analysis of the immature SC markers Ngfr, Ncam1, and L1cam confirms the strong enrichment of immature SCs in the nmSC gate relative to the mSC gate (Figure 2C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Expression of Pou3f1 is elevated in cells of the nmSC gate, but still also to be rather substantial in cells of the mSC gate.
source: In this context, we found expression of Pou3f1 to be elevated in cells of the nmSC gate, but still also to be rather substantial in cells of the mSC gate.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Transcripts of Cdkn1c appear quite selectively enriched in cells of the nmSC gate.
source: Transcripts of Cdkn1c appear quite selectively enriched in cells of the nmSC gate (Figure 2C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Plotting mRNA levels of the myelin genes Mpz, Mbp, and Ncmap revealed the expected enrichment in cells of the mSC gate compared to the nmSC gate.
source: Finally, plotting mRNA levels of the myelin genes Mpz, Mbp, and Ncmap revealed the expected enrichment in cells of the mSC gate compared to the nmSC gate (Figure 2C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The FACS strategy allows the purification of SCs from early postnatal nerves and further enables the collection of two populations enriched in myelinating and not-myelinating cells.
source: Taken together, these data show that our FACS strategy allows the purification of SCs from early postnatal nerves and further enables the collection of two populations enriched in myelinating and not-myelinating cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion statement based on the validation of the FACS strategy.

claim: The possibility of separating myelinating and not-myelinating SCs and obtaining the associated RNA-seq signatures are relevant due to the major transcriptional differences between these two populations of SCs.
source: The possibility of such a separation and obtaining the associated RNA-seq signatures are relevant due to the major transcriptional differences between these two populations of SCs, one that has already activated the myelination program versus the other which contains SCs that are still performing radial sorting of axons (Feltri et al., 2016; Jessen and Mirsky, 2005; Jessen and Mirsky, 2008; Quintes et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Without splitting myelinating and not-myelinating SCs, the RNA-seq data reflect an average signal between the two populations, yielding a convoluted picture of SC transcription dynamics around the onset of myelination.
source: Without such a splitting, the RNA-seq data reflect an average signal between the two populations as seen in the allSC gating strategy that includes all eYFP-positive SCs (Figure 2B,C), yielding a convoluted picture of SC transcription dynamics around the onset of myelination.
evidence: This is an inference about the limitations of not separating SC populations.

claim: The described experimental strategy will be particularly valuable in the evaluation of the molecular phenotypes of mouse mutants that affect axonal radial sorting by SCs and the onset of myelination.
source: We anticipate that the described experimental strategy will be particularly valuable in the evaluation of the molecular phenotypes of mouse mutants that affect axonal radial sorting by SCs and the onset of myelination (Figlia et al., 2017; Gerber et al., 2019; Grove and Brophy, 2014; Nodari et al., 2007; Ommer et al., 2019; Porrello et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculation about the future utility of the experimental strategy, supported by citations.

claim: Analysis of color-coded individual cells per plate of origin indicated homogeneous distribution of cells derived from both plates at P1, P5, and P14.
source: Analysis of color-coded individual cells per plate of origin (designated plate 1 and plate 2, per time point) indicated homogeneous distribution of cells derived from both plates at P1, P5, and P14 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: At P60, a shift in cell distributions according to the origin of the plate was apparent.
source: At P60, a shift in cell distributions according to the origin of the plate was apparent (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Batch correction was applied to the P60 dataset to minimize the bias.
source: Thus, we applied batch correction to this dataset to minimize the bias (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the data processing method used.

claim: Three cell clusters were detected at P1, and four clusters at P5, P14, and P60.
source: Further analysis revealed three cell clusters at P1, and four clusters at P5, P14, and P60, which are individually color-coded on tSNE projections per time point in (Figure 3A,C,E,G).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3A,C,E,G.

claim: A proliferating SC cluster was detected at P1, P5 and P14, containing cells that express Mki67 and Top2a.
source: We detected a proliferating SC cluster (marked prol. SC) at P1, P5 and P14, containing cells that express Mki67 and Top2a (Figure 3B,D,F).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3B,D,F.

claim: Some SCs expressing Mki67 and Top2a were also found in the non-myelinating (Remak) cell clusters at P60.
source: Some SCs expressing these markers were also found in the non-myelinating (Remak) cell clusters (marked nm(R)SC) at P60, consistent with previous findings (Stierli et al., 2018; Figure 3G,H).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and data shown in Figure 3G,H.

claim: Immature SCs formed a cluster at P1 and P5, characterized by expression of Ngfr, Ncam1, and L1cam.
source: Immature SCs (marked iSC) also formed a cluster at P1 and P5, characterized by expression of Ngfr, Ncam1, and L1cam (Figure 3B,D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3B,D.

claim: The same markers (Ngfr, Ncam1, and L1cam) are also enriched in Remak SCs undergoing maturation at P14 and as mature Remak SCs at P60.
source: The same markers are also enriched in Remak SCs undergoing maturation at P14 (Figure 3F), designated as transition SCs (marked tSC), and as mature Remak SCs (marked nm(R)SC) at P60 (Figure 3H)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3F,H.

claim: A cluster of pro-myelinating SCs could be detected at P1, P5, and P14, with enriched expression of Pou3f1 and Cdkn1c.
source: A cluster of pro-myelinating SCs (marked pmSCs) could be detected at P1, P5, and P14, with enriched expression of Pou3f1 and Cdkn1c (Figure 3B,D,F).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3B,D,F.

claim: At P1, the pro-myelinating SC cluster also contains SCs expressing Mpz, Mbp, and Ncmap.
source: At P1, this cluster also contains SCs expressing Mpz, Mbp, and Ncmap (Figure 3B)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Cells expressing Mpz, Mbp, and Ncmap at P5, P14, and P60 are strongly enriched in myelinating SC clusters.
source: while cells expressing these transcripts at later time points (P5, P14, and P60) are strongly enriched in myelinating SC clusters (marked mSC) (Figure 3D,F,H).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3D,F,H.

claim: At P60, data processing suggested two clusters labeled by myelinating SC markers and two clusters labeled by non-myelinating (Remak) SC markers.
source: At P60, data processing suggested two clusters labeled by myelinating SC markers and two clusters labeled by non-myelinating (Remak) SC markers (Figure 3G,H).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3G,H.

claim: The combined-data tSNE plot resulted in one tSNE plot of cells from all time points.
source: To obtain a more integrated perspective of transcriptomic dynamics over postnatal SC differentiation, we combined all data obtained by single-cell SC sequencing in an integrated analysis. This strategy resulted in one tSNE plot of cells from all time points (Figure 4A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Mapping the cellular transcript expression of selected differentiation marker genes within the combined-data plot revealed a close association of clusters with known key stages of SC differentiation.
source: Mapping the cellular transcript expression of selected differentiation marker genes within the combined-data plot revealed a close association of clusters with known key stages of SC differentiation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Color-coding individual cells according to the age of origin generated a chronological gradient over the tSNE plot that agrees with the pattern of overlapped marker transcripts and the two differentiation paths.
source: Color-coding individual cells according to the age of origin generated a chronological gradient over the tSNE plot that agrees with the pattern of overlapped marker transcripts and the two differentiation paths (Figure 4C)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: SCs derived from nerves of younger animals correspond to earlier stages of cell differentiation than those obtained from older mice.
source: SCs derived from nerves of younger animals correspond to earlier stages of cell differentiation than those obtained from older mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The putative non-myelinating SC maturation path includes two informatic clusters, one enriched in P14 SCs and the other in P60 SCs, which may reflect temporal snapshots of the maturation fate of non-myelinating (Remak) SCs.
source: On a discussion note, the putative non-myelinating SC maturation path includes two informatic clusters, one enriched in P14 SCs (marked tSC) and the other in P60 SCs (marked nm(R)SC). These findings may reflect temporal snapshots of the maturation fate of non-myelinating (Remak) SCs.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data by the authors.

claim: The informatically predicted mSC clusters are differentially enriched in mSCs of progressing mouse ages, potentially reflecting the particular requirements of early and young adult phases of the myelination program.
source: Likewise, the informatically predicted mSC clusters are differentially enriched in mSCs of progressing mouse ages, potentially reflecting the particular requirements of early and young adult phases of the myelination program.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data by the authors.

claim: A supervised Slingshot trajectory and pseudotime inference approach was applied to visualize the development of transcript levels along the two SC differentiation and maturation trajectories.
source: To aid visualizing the development of transcript levels along the two SC differentiation and maturation trajectories as suggested by the combined-data tSNE plot, we applied a supervised Slingshot trajectory and pseudotime inference approach (Street et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the analytical method used, supported by a citation.

claim: The Slingshot analysis indicated a bifurcated projection that splits in two major branches after the iSC cluster, one leading toward the myelinating fate and the other toward non-myelinating (Remak) SC specification.
source: As expected, the results of this approach indicated a bifurcated projection that splits in two major branches after the iSC cluster, one leading toward the myelinating fate and the other toward non-myelinating (Remak) SC specification (Figure 4D)
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Transcripts of Ncam1 get strongly reduced with differentiation on the myelinating trajectory, but remain high along the non-myelinating trajectory.
source: For example as expected, transcripts of Ncam1 get strongly reduced with differentiation on the myelinating trajectory, but remain high along the non-myelinating trajectory.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The transcripts Pou3f1 and Cdkn1c are prominently enriched along the myelinating trajectory in a transient manner.
source: The transcripts Pou3f1 and Cdkn1c are prominently enriched along the myelinating trajectory in a transient manner (Figure 4E).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Transcripts for Mpz are accumulated along the myelinating trajectory, albeit also detected at lower levels in all other SC clusters.
source: Furthermore, transcripts for Mpz are accumulated along the myelinating trajectory, albeit also detected at lower levels in all other SC clusters.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Transcripts for Ncmap are more restricted to late stages of the myelinating trajectory.
source: In comparison, transcripts for Ncmap are more restricted to late stages of the myelinating trajectory (Figure 4E).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The Smart-Seq2 single-cell RNA sequencing dataset provides a connected collection of clusters along key stages of SC postnatal differentiation.
source: Taken together, our Smart-Seq2 single-cell RNA sequencing dataset provides a connected collection of clusters along key stages of SC postnatal differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the dataset.

claim: The dataset enables a direct comparison, with single-cell resolution, of the differential transcriptome changes throughout SC maturation during postnatal development.
source: Furthermore, the dataset enables a direct comparison, with single-cell resolution, of the differential transcriptome changes throughout SC maturation during postnatal development.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the dataset.

claim: Various other cell types besides SCs and neurons/axons contribute together to the optimal function of peripheral nerves.
source: Various other cell types besides SCs and neurons/axons contribute together to the optimal function of peripheral nerves.
evidence: This is a general statement about peripheral nerve biology.

claim: Understanding of the individual roles of different cell types in nerve development and homeostasis is limited.
source: However, our understanding of the individual roles of these different cell types in nerve development and homeostasis are limited.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: There is a crucial interplay between macrophages, endoneurial fibroblast-like cells, and SCs in fostering axonal regeneration between proximal and distal nerve stumps after nerve transection.
source: This knowledge includes a crucial interplay between macrophages, endoneurial fibroblast-like cells, and SCs in fostering axonal regeneration between proximal and distal nerve stumps after nerve transection (Cattin et al., 2015; Cattin and Lloyd, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Cattin et al., 2015; Cattin and Lloyd, 2016.

claim: Nerve-resident Pdgfra-expressing cells serve as a cellular reservoir during regeneration after toe tip amputation of adult mice.
source: Furthermore, nerve-resident Pdgfra-expressing cells (which include cells of the endoneurium, perineurium, and epineurium) have been shown to serve as a cellular reservoir during regeneration after toe tip amputation of adult mice (Carr et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Carr et al., 2019.

claim: The study used 10x Genomics technology rather than Smart-seq2 for analyzing all nerve cells because higher cell throughput is required to characterize adequately the heterogeneous cell types expected in the sciatic nerve.
source: We chose to use the 10x Genomics technology rather than Smart-seq2 for this part of our study, since higher cell throughput is required to characterize adequately the heterogeneous cell types expected in the sciatic nerve.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the methodological choice made in the study.

claim: Approximately 4000 sorted nerve cells were loaded into the Chromium controller for separation of single cells into droplets during each individual run.
source: Approximately 4000 sorted nerve cells were loaded into the Chromium controller for separation of single cells into droplets during each individual run, with cDNA and libraries prepared according to 10x Genomics recommendations (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental procedure.

claim: Three independent samples were included for each time point, processed as three independent 10x Genomics runs.
source: To account for biological variability and to control for technical bias, we included three independent samples for each time point, processed as three independent 10x Genomics runs (designated as Run 1, 2, and 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design.

claim: Each sample consisted of a nerve cell suspension extracted from male and female mice in a 1:1 ratio.
source: Each sample consisted of a nerve cell suspension extracted from male and female mice in a 1:1 ratio.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental design.

claim: Cells from all three runs are contributing to the formation of each cluster, indicating no major bias.
source: Color-coding of the cells in the tSNE plot (Supplementary file 2) according to different runs revealed no major bias, as cells from all three runs are contributing to the formation of each cluster (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Analysis of the P60 single-cell RNA-seq data revealed nine clusters.
source: Analysis of the P60 single-cell RNA-seq data revealed nine clusters (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: SCs accounted for 414 out of 12428 cells (3.3%) at P60.
source: SCs accounted for 414 out of 12428 cells (3.3%; note that this number is affected by the experimental extraction efficiency and does not reflect the proportion of SCs present in adult sciatic nerves [Stierli et al., 2018]), formed a single cluster (marked SC) in the tSNE, and were characterized by Sox10 (encoding the transcription factor SOX10) expression (Finzsch et al., 2010; Jessen et al., 2015; Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data and citations.

claim: The SC cluster at P60 shows a remarkable regional distribution of myelinating SCs on one side and non-myelinating (Remak) SCs on the opposite side.
source: However, closer inspection revealed a remarkable regional distribution of myelinating SCs (marked mSC) on one side of the cluster and non-myelinating (Remak) SCs on the opposite side (marked nm(R)SC) (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: Expression of the myelin genes Mpz, Mbp, and Ncmap is enriched in the mSC region of the cluster, whereas Ngfr and Ncam1 expression are enriched in the nm(R)SC area of the cluster.
source: Expression of the myelin genes Mpz, Mbp, and Ncmap is enriched in the mSC region of the cluster, whereas Ngfr and Ncam1 expression are enriched in the nm(R)SC area of the cluster (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: Enriched Pdgfra expression labeled clusters of epineurial, perineurial, and endoneurial fibroblast-like nerve cells.
source: As previously shown (Carr et al., 2019), enriched Pdgfra expression labeled clusters of epineurial (marked EpC), perineurial (marked PnC), and endoneurial fibroblast-like (marked EnC) nerve cells
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Expression of Cd34 labels epineurial, perineurial, and endoneurial cells, and additionally also endothelial cell clusters.
source: whereas expression of Cd34 (encoding Hematopoietic Progenitor Cell Antigen CD34) labels all of the above (albeit the perineurial cell cluster only weakly), and additionally also endothelial cell clusters (Carr et al., 2019; Richard et al., 2012; Richard et al., 2014; Figure 5A,E).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 5A,E.

claim: Enriched expression of Pcolce2 and Ly6c1 label the epineurial cell cluster.
source: Enriched expression of Pcolce2 (encoding Procollagen C-Endopeptidase Enhancer 2) and Ly6c1 (encoding lymphocyte antigen 6 complex, locus C1) label the epineurial cell cluster (Figure 5E; Carr et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The perineurial cell cluster is labeled by expression of Itgb4 and Slc2a1.
source: The perineurial cell cluster is labeled by expression of Itgb4 (encoding Integrin Subunit Beta 4) and Slc2a1 (encoding Solute Carrier Family 2 Member 1, also commonly known as Glucose Transporter Type 1(Glut1)) (Figure 5E; Carr et al., 2019; Niessen et al., 1994; Takebe et al., 2008; Tserentsoodol et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The endoneurial fibroblast-like cell cluster is characterized by enriched expression of Col2a1 and Sox9.
source: Finally, the endoneurial fibroblast-like cell cluster is characterized by enriched expression of Col2a1 (encoding Collagen Type II Alpha 1 Chain) and Sox9 (encoding the transcription factor SOX9) (Figure 5E; Carr et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The immune cell cluster can be recognized by Ptprc expression and particularly high abundance of the macrophage marker Cd68.
source: The immune cell cluster (marked IC) can be recognized by Ptprc (encoding Protein Tyrosine Phosphatase Receptor Type C, also commonly known as CD45) expression and particularly high abundance of the macrophage marker Cd68 (encoding Scavenger Receptor Class D, Member 1) (Figure 5F; Carr et al., 2019; Cattin et al., 2015; Hidmark et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Two clusters are characterized by ample expression of Pecam1 but not of Pdgfrb, and were classified as bona fide endothelial cell clusters.
source: Two clusters are characterized by ample expression of Pecam1 (Platelet And Endothelial Cell Adhesion Molecule 1, also commonly known as CD31) (Figure 5G; Carr et al., 2019; Cattin et al., 2015; Stierli et al., 2018), but not of Pdgfrb (encoding Platelet Derived Growth Factor Receptor Beta) (Figure 5H). We classified these groups as bona fide endothelial cell clusters.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 5G,H.

claim: One endothelial cluster was more enriched in Cldn5 and Slc2a1 expression (marked EC1).
source: From these two clusters, one was more enriched in Cldn5 (encoding the tight junction component Claudin 5) (Pummi et al., 2004; Figure 5G) and Slc2a1 (Takebe et al., 2008; Tserentsoodol et al., 1999; Figure 5E) expression (marked EC1).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 5E,G.

claim: The other endothelial cluster had lower expression of Cldn5 and Slc2a1, together with higher abundance of the endothelial marker Cd300lg (marked EC2).
source: The other endothelial cluster had lower expression of Cldn5 and Slc2a1 (Figure 5E,G), together with higher abundance of the endothelial marker Cd300lg (encoding CD300 Molecule Like Family Member G) (Figure 5G; Zhao et al., 2018) (marked EC2).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and data shown in Figure 5E,G.

claim: The two observed endothelial clusters may relate to different sets of endothelial cells, with different functional properties associated with vessels with different physical and physiological features.
source: One might speculate that the two observed endothelial clusters may relate to different sets of endothelial cells, with different functional properties associated with vessels with different physical and physiological features.
evidence: This is a speculation by the authors about the meaning of the two endothelial clusters.

claim: A cluster labeled by expression of Acta2 and Pdgfrb was identified as pericytes and vascular smooth muscle cells.
source: Next, a cluster labeled by expression of Acta2 (encoding Actin Alpha 2, Smooth Muscle) and Pdgfrb was identified as pericytes and vascular smooth muscle cells (marked Per/VSMC) (Figure 5H; Carr et al., 2019; Stierli et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: The remaining discernible cluster contains cells that are simultaneously positive for Pecam1 and Pdgfrb (marked Per/EC*).
source: Finally, the remaining discernible cluster of this blood vessel-associated group contains cells that are simultaneously positive for Pecam1 and Pdgfrb (Figure 5G,H), canonical markers for endothelial cells and pericytes, respectively (marked Per/EC*).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5G,H.

claim: The Per/EC* cluster is more likely to derive from 'cell doublets' between endothelial cells and pericytes, and thus is a technical artefact potentially fostered by the close physical interactions between pericytes and endothelial cells on vessels.
source: However, we consider it more likely that this cluster derives from 'cell doublets' between endothelial cells and pericytes, and thus is a technical artefact potentially fostered by the close physical interactions between pericytes and endothelial cells on vessels, a connection that may not have been broken sufficiently by our nerve dissociation procedure.
evidence: This is an interpretation by the authors about the likely origin of the Per/EC* cluster.

claim: Analysis of developing nerves at P1 resulted in a tSNE projection containing 11 clusters.
source: Our complementary analysis of developing nerves at P1 resulted in a tSNE projection containing 11 clusters (Figure 6A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: At P1, the SC cluster included a larger number and fraction of SCs than obtained at P60 (3175 or 28% (P1), vs. 414 or 3.3% (P60)), likely reflecting a more efficient extraction of intact SCs from P1 nerves.
source: Notably, even after the previously described negative selection by FACS, the P1 SC cluster still included a larger number and fraction of SCs than obtained at P60 (3175 or 28% (P1), vs. 414 or 3.3% (P60)), likely reflecting a more efficient extraction of intact SCs from P1 nerves.
evidence: This statement includes data and an interpretation about extraction efficiency.

claim: Three SC clusters were identified by Sox10 expression at P1.
source: Three SC clusters were identified by Sox10 expression (Figure 6B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The SC clusters at P1 are highly enriched in Mpz, Mbp, and Ncmap transcripts.
source: As a group, they are also highly enriched in Mpz, Mbp, and Ncmap transcripts.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Ncmap expression is most prominent in a SC cluster that reflects most likely pro-myelinating SCs at P1.
source: Ncmap expression is most prominent in a SC cluster that reflects most likely pro-myelinating SCs (marked pmSC) at this age (Figure 6B), although a few SCs might also be included here that have already started to produce myelin.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: An overlapping neighboring group at P1, labeled by Ncam1 and Ngfr expression, includes immature SCs.
source: An overlapping neighboring group, labeled by Ncam1 and Ngfr expression, includes immature SCs (marked by iSC) (Figure 6B), some of which also expressing the proliferation markers Mki67 and Top2a (marked prol. SC) (Figure 6C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: The expression of proliferation markers at P1 labels also other proliferating cells, which were tentatively designated as a cluster of proliferating fibroblast-like cells due to the expression of Pdgfra.
source: The expression of these proliferation markers labels also other proliferating cells in P1 nerves, which we tentatively designated as a cluster of proliferating fibroblast-like cells (marked prol. Fb) due to the expression of Pdgfra (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: Assignments of clusters at P1 have to be considered tentative, since the marker genes used for the assignments are likely expressed at different levels than at P60 due to the different cell differentiation states.
source: In this context, we note again that these detailed assignments have to be considered tentative at this time, since the marker genes used for the assignments at P1 are likely expressed at different levels than at P60 due to the different cell differentiation states.
evidence: This is a cautionary note by the authors about the interpretation of the P1 data.

claim: The fibroblast-related cluster (FbRel*) includes cells in which, besides Pdgfra, a peculiar set of transcripts are quite prominent, including some cells expressing markers more enriched in other clusters, and even some cells expressing genes typical of the SC lineage.
source: The fibroblast-related cluster (FbRel*) includes cells in which, besides Pdgfra, a peculiar set of transcripts are quite prominent, including some cells expressing markers more enriched in other clusters, and even some cells expressing genes typical of the SC lineage, including Mbp, Mpz, and Sox10 (Figure 6B,D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 6B,D.

claim: Determination of the origins and validation of the FbRel* cluster requires further investigations.
source: Determination of the origins and validation of this cluster requires further investigations.
evidence: This is a statement about the need for future work to understand the FbRel* cluster.

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing of all-included sciatic nerves with 10x genomics provided transcriptome profiles on most of the major cell types that are expected to reside in mouse sciatic nerves, both in early postnatal development and in young adults.
source: In summary, single-cell RNA sequencing of all-included sciatic nerves with 10x genomics provided transcriptome profiles on most of the major cell types that are expected to reside in mouse sciatic nerves, both in early postnatal development and in young adults.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the results of the 10x genomics analysis.

claim: Epineurial adipocytes were not detected as a separate cluster in the 10x genomics analysis.
source: One notable exception are epineurial adipocytes (Montani et al., 2018), which we did not detect as a separate cluster.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of the analysis, supported by a citation.

claim: A few cells expressing adipocyte markers can be found within the P60 epineurial cells cluster, but it remains unclear whether they represent bona fide epineurial adipocytes.
source: A few cells expressing adipocyte markers, including Car3 (encoding Carbonic Anhydrase 3), Cdo1 (encoding Cysteine Dioxygenase Type 1), Adipoq (encoding Adiponectin), and Plin1 (encoding Perilipin 1) (Burl et al., 2018; Deng et al., 2015), can be found within the P60 epineurial cells cluster (see SNAT), but it remains unclear at this time whether they represent bona fide epineurial adipocytes.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations and indicates uncertainty about the identity of these cells.

claim: A small group of cells with expression of markers of lymphatic endothelial cells can be found within one of the P60 endothelial cell clusters, but they have not been allocated as separate cluster potentially due to their scarcity.
source: Another peculiar example are cells that line potentially lymphatic vessels. A small group of cells with expression of markers of lymphatic endothelial cells including Prox1 (encoding the transcription factor Prox-1), Flt4 (encoding VEGF Receptor-3), and Lyve1 (encoding Lymphatic Vessel Endothelial Hyaluronan Receptor 1) (Wigle et al., 2002) can be found within one of the P60 endothelial cell cluster (endothelial cell cluster marked EC2; see SNAT), but they have not been allocated as separate cluster potentially due to their scarcity.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and indicates a limitation of the clustering analysis.

claim: The approach of using dissociation of cells from nerves followed by FACS has the limitation of some potential subsampling of a subset of cells.
source: We note that the approach of using dissociation of cells from nerves followed by FACS has the limitation of some potential subsampling of a subset of cells (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of the experimental approach.

claim: SCs isolated from extensively myelinated nerves might not reveal the full diversity spectrum.
source: In particular, SCs isolated from extensively myelinated nerves might not reveal the full diversity spectrum.
evidence: This is a statement about a potential limitation of the SC isolation approach.

claim: The observed low relative extraction efficiency of SCs may reflect different sensitivities of distinct SC populations to the experimental procedures, associated with the potential of subsampling.
source: The observed low relative extraction efficiency in this context may reflect different sensitivities of distinct SC populations to the experimental procedures, associated with the potential of subsampling.
evidence: This is an interpretation by the authors about the reasons for low extraction efficiency.

claim: The validated datasets presented in this study are intended to serve as a reference point of gene expression in peripheral nerves.
source: Taken together, the validated datasets presented in this study are intended to serve as a reference point of gene expression in peripheral nerves, obtained by various complementary forms of RNA sequencing techniques.
evidence: This is a statement about the intended use of the datasets.

claim: The multilayered approach allowed both the coverage and emphasis on SCs and other major populations of resident cells in sciatic nerves, mainly focused on postnatal development.
source: Our multilayered approach allowed both the coverage and emphasis on SCs and other major populations of resident cells in sciatic nerves, mainly focused on postnatal development.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the scope of the study.

claim: The data have been integrated in a freely accessible and searchable web interface (https://www.snat.ethz.ch).
source: We have integrated our data in a freely accessible and searchable web interface (https://www.snat.ethz.ch) with the intention to make a contribution to the filling of a gap in current peripheral nerve research.
evidence: This is a statement about the data availability and intended contribution.

claim: There will be expanding efforts to cover various aspects of peripheral nerve biology such as in cellular-, injury-, aging-, and disease models.
source: Using this resource as baseline, together with recently published complementary extensions mainly focusing on immune cells in peripheral nerves (Kalinski et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2020; Ydens et al., 2020) and adult nerves (Wolbert et al., 2020), we anticipate that there will be expanding efforts to cover various aspects of peripheral nerve biology such as in cellular-, injury-, aging-, and disease models (Toma et al., 2020) as well as covering other related glia cells (Avraham et al., 2020; Stierli et al., 2019), hopefully yielding insightful and valuable data as the fundamental basis of building and testing hypothesis in functional follow-up studies.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions, supported by citations.
